{{Sources exist|date=October 2024}}
In [[category theory]], a '''premonoidal category<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Anderson |first1=S.O. |last2=Power |first2=A.J. |date=April 1997 |title=A representable approach to finite nondeterminism |journal=Theoretical Computer Science |volume=177 |issue=1 |pages=3–25 |doi=10.1016/s0304-3975(96)00232-0 |issn=0304-3975|doi-access=free }}</ref>''' is a generalisation of a [[monoidal category]] where the monoidal product need not be a [[bifunctor]],  but only to be functorial in its two arguments separately. This is in analogy with the concept of [[separate continuity]] in [[topology]].

Premonoidal categories naturally arise in theoretical [[computer science]] as the [[Kleisli category|Kleisli categories]] of [[strong monad]]s.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Power |first1=John |last2=Robinson |first2=Edmund |date=October 1997 |title=Premonoidal categories and notions of computation |url=https://www.cambridge.org/core/product/identifier/S0960129597002375/type/journal_article |journal=Mathematical Structures in Computer Science |language=en |volume=7 |issue=5 |pages=453–468 |doi=10.1017/S0960129597002375 |issn=0960-1295|url-access=subscription }}</ref> They also have a graphical language given by [[string diagram]]s with an extra wire going through each box so that they cannot be reordered.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Jeffrey |first=Alan |date=1998 |title=Premonoidal categories and flow graphs |journal=Electronic Notes in Theoretical Computer Science |volume=10 |pages=51 |doi=10.1016/s1571-0661(05)80688-7 |issn=1571-0661|doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Jeffrey |first=Alan |date=1997 |title=Premonoidal categories and a graphical view of programs |url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/228639836}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Román |first=Mario |date=2023-08-07 |title=Promonads and String Diagrams for Effectful Categories |journal=Electronic Proceedings in Theoretical Computer Science |volume=380 |pages=344–361 |doi=10.4204/EPTCS.380.20 |arxiv=2205.07664 |issn=2075-2180}}</ref>

== Funny tensor product ==
The [[category of small categories]] <math>\mathbf{Cat}</math> is a [[closed monoidal category]] in exactly two ways: with the usual [[categorical product]] and with the '''funny tensor product'''.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Foltz |first1=F. |last2=Lair |first2=C. |last3=Kelly |first3=G. M. |date=1980-05-01 |title=Algebraic categories with few monoidal biclosed structures or none |url=https://dx.doi.org/10.1016/0022-4049%2880%2990082-1 |journal=Journal of Pure and Applied Algebra |volume=17 |issue=2 |pages=171–177 |doi=10.1016/0022-4049(80)90082-1 |issn=0022-4049|url-access=subscription }}</ref> Given two categories <math>C</math> and <math>D</math>, let <math>C \Rightarrow D</math> be the category with [[functor]]s <math>F, G : C \to D</math> as objects and '''unnatural transformations''' <math>\alpha : F \Rightarrow G</math> as arrows, i.e. families of morphisms <math>\{ \alpha_X : F(X) \to G(X) \}_{X \in C}</math> which do not necessarily satisfy the condition for a [[natural transformation]].

The funny tensor product is the [[Adjunction (category theory)|left adjoint]] of unnatural transformations, i.e. there is a [[natural isomorphism]] <math>\mathbf{Cat}(C \ \Box \ D, D') \simeq \mathbf{Cat}(C, D \Rightarrow D' )</math> for [[currying]]. It can be defined explicitly as the [[Pushout (category theory)|pushout]] of the [[Span (category theory)|span]] <math>(C_0 \times D) \to (C \times D) \leftarrow (C \times D_0)</math> where <math>C_0, D_0</math> are the [[Discrete category|discrete categories]] of objects of <math>C, D</math> and the two functors are inclusions. In the case of groups seen as one-object categories, this is called the [[free product]].

== Sesquicategories ==
The same way we can define a monoidal category as a one-object [[2-category]], i.e. an [[enriched category]] over <math>(\mathbf{Cat}, \times)</math> with the Cartesian product as monoidal structure, we can define a premonoidal category as a one-object '''sesquicategory''',<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Stell |first=John |date=1994 |title=Modelling Term Rewriting Systems by Sesqui-Categories |url=https://ncatlab.org/nlab/files/Stell.pdf |journal=Proc. Catégories, Algèbres, Esquisses et Néo-Esquisses}}</ref> i.e. a category enriched over <math>(\mathbf{Cat}, \Box)</math> with the funny tensor product as monoidal structure. This is called a sesquicategory (literally, "one-and-a-half category") because it is like a 2-category without the interchange law <math>(\alpha\circ_0\beta)\circ_1(\gamma\circ_0\delta) = (\alpha\circ_1\gamma)\circ_0(\beta\circ_1\delta)</math>.
